briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 7, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis, A Global Warning
sections.content: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has warned that severe wildfires and heatwaves are occurring globally, threatening efforts to improve air quality [1, 9, 32, 147]. In particular, due to the strongest El Niño phenomenon in 1,000 years, even more intense heatwaves and floods are expected next year [4], raising concerns that global warming may already exceed the 1.5°C critical threshold [125, 136]. In Nepal, a $2.5 billion flood disaster occurred, leading to the declaration of a national day of mourning and a request for climate change fund support from the international community [26, 34, 116, 138, 144, 145], starkly revealing the reality of the climate crisis. Domestically, Jeju experienced a complex combination of heatwaves, droughts, heavy rainfall, and high water temperatures in the summer of 2026, leaving a warning [29], and the Gyeongnam region is also paying the 'climate change bill' with its worst heatwaves and torrential rains [14, 115].

sections.title: ⚠️ Testing Domestic Society's Climate Resilience
sections.content: Climate change is exposing various vulnerabilities across domestic society. Concerns have been raised that flight disruptions may increase due to heatwaves and storms [5], and fishermen in Boryeong are appealing for help due to difficulties caused by climate change and sales channel issues [23]. An analysis also suggested that insurance companies are falling into 'self-contradiction' and 'karma' due to the climate crisis [3, 19]. Public health and safety issues are also serious; the Gwangju region is seeking 'climate health' solutions in response to the normalization of heatwaves, heavy rainfall, and droughts [12, 30], and the Seoul Metropolitan Council urged thorough monitoring of 'Arisu' water quality safety and hygiene during heatwaves [18]. The damage suffered by construction site workers from heatwaves and the high perceived temperature for sanitation workers demonstrate that extreme heat is becoming a matter of survival [114, 115].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Domestic and International Efforts for Carbon Neutrality Transition
sections.content: Efforts across various sectors of society to respond to the climate crisis are accelerating. The Climate Change Center is embarking on a new journey as the 'Climate Change Foundation' after 18 years, strengthening its public role [2, 10], and the Daejeon Seogu Council adopted a proposal to strengthen safety management of road facilities in response to climate change [17, 20, 35]. In Suseong-gu, environmental education on 'Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality' was conducted for public officials [22, 25, 28], and Naju City is spreading carbon neutrality practices in daily life through a tumbler usage campaign [46, 48]. In Gurye-gun, preparations for the '2026 Carbon Neutral Soil Revitalization Expo' are in full swing [38, 55, 73, 77, 82], and Jeongeup rural leaders have initiated agricultural waste collection activities to practice carbon neutrality in farming fields [60, 66, 75, 78, 84]. In the industrial sector, Hyundai Steel's US steel mill achieved a world-first 70% reduction in carbon emissions [39, 80, 87], and a Wonkwang University research team is accelerating the development of microorganism-nano convergence 'carbon-neutral smart construction materials' [68, 88].

sections.title: 🌱 Expanding Renewable Energy and Securing Future Economic Drivers
sections.content: The global trend towards renewable energy transition is accelerating, leading to new economic opportunities. According to a UN report, investing $1 in clean air and climate change cooperation measures can generate $15 in economic benefits [119, 122, 127, 143]. Chinese solar products are dominating the African market with their price competitiveness, eroding demand for fossil fuels [91], and in the United States, the cost of power generation combining renewable energy and energy storage systems (ESS) has dropped to a level similar to gas power, making the perception of 'expensive' a thing of the past [109]. Domestically, 'Renewable Energy Special Leading Complexes' will be established in mega-special zones, opening the way for direct power transactions between companies [92], and the Korea Energy Agency has presented a roadmap for expanding renewable energy [93, 98, 100]. Yeoju City is seeking solutions for managing reckless solar development ahead of the implementation of the 'Renewable Energy Act' [96, 97, 99, 104, 106, 110], and the Korea Water Resources Corporation held an explanatory session on RE100 implementation support and national carbon neutrality policy promotion [112].

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Action and New Challenges
sections.content: The international community continues various discussions and actions to address the climate crisis. Early maturation of European crops due to climate change is being observed [118, 135], and French wine production is also facing a crisis due to climate change [142]. Pacific island nations are strongly demanding clean energy and financial support at COP31 [126], and the European Union (EU) is strengthening environmental regulations, including pursuing restrictions on waste exports [113]. In New Zealand, a new bill abolishing climate torts to exempt responsibility for climate change impacts has emerged [139], demonstrating the diversification of international legal approaches to climate. Adaptation cases are also spreading, such as New York's Central Park making efforts to adapt to climate change [132], and the American village of Salem relocating to higher ground due to climate change [133].

briefing.closing: Through the climate-related news collected today, we have been able to confirm the severity of the climate crisis, along with the multifaceted domestic and international efforts to overcome it. Continued interest and action will determine our future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
